title: Nonlinear optical responses of semiconducting graphene nanoribbons: Strong constraint from a hidden symmetry
authors: Jiawei Ruan, Weichen Tang, Yang-Hao Chan, Chen Hu, Xiaoxun Gong, Steven G. Louie
abstract: Nonlinear optical (NLO) responses are powerful tools for probing material structures, as they are highly sensitive to spatial symmetries. For instance, it is well known that having inversion symmetry forbids even-order NLO effects. Here, we show that nonspatial symmetries can also significantly constrain NLO responses. In graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) with bipartite-lattice structures, we identify the approximate bipartite-lattice particle-hole (BLPH) symmetry strongly suppresses even-order NLO effects, even for systems with no inversion symmetry. Importantly, we demonstrate that this approximate symmetry enables the optical generation of nearly pure spin shift currents in ferromagnetic GNRs, with the charge shift currents strongly suppressed. The spin orientation of these photo-induced DC spin currents can be easily tuned by an external magnetic field, providing distinct advantages over previous schemes for generating pure spin shift currents in antiferromagnetic systems. We illustrate our findings using a recently synthesized ferromagnetic Janus GNR. Our results underscore the significance of an overlooked symmetry aspect of NLO responses and highlight magnetic GNRs as promising candidates for spintronic devices.
summary: This work reveals that hidden, nonspatial symmetries, particularly the bipartite-lattice particle-hole symmetry, impose strong constraints on nonlinear optical responses in graphene nanoribbons. This symmetry causes the suppression of even-order NLO effects and, crucially, enables the efficient, field-tunable generation of pure spin currents in magnetic GNRs.
main_problem: The paper investigates how nonspatial symmetries, specifically the approximate bipartite-lattice particle-hole (BLPH) symmetry, constrain nonlinear optical (NLO) responses in graphene nanoribbons (GNRs).
main_result: The BLPH symmetry strongly suppresses even-order NLO effects, even when inversion symmetry is absent, and enables the optical generation of nearly pure spin shift currents in ferromagnetic GNRs.
method: The analysis uses the quantum kinetic equation for the density matrix, deriving symmetry relations from the Hamiltonian properties to predict vanishing contributions to even-order current densities.
model_or_system: The study focuses on semiconducting Graphene Nanoribbons (GNRs) with bipartite-lattice structures, extending to ferromagnetic Janus GNRs. The theoretical framework involves tight-binding models and symmetry analysis using operations like chiral and particle-hole symmetry.
key_observables: Nonlinear optical responses (SHG, HHG), charge shift currents, and spin shift currents.
important_parameters: The degree of symmetry preservation (approximate BLPH symmetry), external magnetic field strength, and the lattice structure (bipartite).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the independent-particle approximation and the assumption of approximate preservation of the BLPH symmetry in real systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the vanishing of even-order current contributions due to symmetry, show band structures for ideal and perturbed GNRs, and compare charge vs. spin current generation in magnetic systems.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes symmetry constraints on NLO responses, first establishing the general principle of symmetry suppression in bipartite lattices, then applying this to nonmagnetic GNRs, and finally demonstrating the unique generation of pure spin currents in ferromagnetic GNRs.
why_interesting: The deep connection between fundamental lattice symmetries (like particle-hole symmetry) and measurable optical responses (NLO effects) provides a powerful, symmetry-based tool for designing spintronic materials.
